d: Deep-space mechanical civilizations, solar chromosphere explorations, and cosmic diaspora by Gregory Benford, David Brin, and Walter M. Miller Jr.

sagittarius-a-star.x: Supermassive core of the Milky Way where ancient self-replicating machine intelligences dominate stellar systems and hunt organic biological civilizations.
sagittarius-a-star.a: mech mantle capellin killeen core machine

gaia-3796072592206250624.x: Red dwarf Ross 128 system where human interstellar explorers encounter the remnants of an extraterrestrial technological biosphere and aggressive machine probes.
gaia-3796072592206250624.a: snark ocean of night nigel walmsley machine probe

mercury.x: Heavily shielded subterranean polar station on Mercury coordinating human and alien expeditions diving deep into the solar chromosphere.

sol.x: Lower chromosphere of the Sun explored by refrigerator-ships discovering anomalous indigenous plasma-based lifeforms dubbed Sun-Ghosts.

hip-71683.x: Alpha Centauri destination of the starship Stella Maris, launched by the Order of Saint Leibowitz carrying the memorabilia of human knowledge as Earth undergoes nuclear immolation.

b.s: Spanning Gregory Benford’s Galactic Center saga depicting humanity’s struggle against mechanical intelligences at Sagittarius A* and Ross 128, David Brin’s expedition into Sol’s chromosphere in Sundiver, and the starship Stella Maris fleeing atomic war for Alpha Centauri in A Canticle for Leibowitz.
b.a: Gregory Benford, David Brin, Walter M. Miller Jr.
b.r: In the Ocean of Night (1977), Sundiver (1980), and A Canticle for Leibowitz (1960)
